name: Queen Charlotte Track
region: Queen Charlotte Sound / Tōtaranui, Marlborough Sounds
why: Four days along the bays and ridges between Queen Charlotte and Kenepuru sounds, from Cook's anchorage at Ship Cove to Anakiwa, with lodges or campsites each night.
book: Boat from Picton to Meretoto/Ship Cove (no road); boats can carry your pack between lodges. A Queen Charlotte Track Land Cooperative pass is needed for the private land from Kenepuru Saddle to Anakiwa. DOC campsites must be booked all year; lodges book direct. Bus or boat back from Anakiwa.
water: Taps at DOC campsites, untreated: boil, filter or treat. Some ridge sections are dry in summer: carry water for the day.
dangers: Tight blind corners shared with mountain bikers, steep drops beside the track and slippery clay when wet.
Camp Bay to Torea Saddle is long (24.5 km, about 8 h) on an exposed ridge.
Wasps in late summer and autumn: carry antihistamine if allergic.
Fallen trees and slips after storms; the track can close in extreme drought.
turnaround: Each road saddle (Kenepuru, Torea, Te Mahia) is an exit: if you are behind schedule or the weather turns, finish the day there and take a road or boat transfer.

points.name: Meretoto / Ship Cove
points.note: Boat landing only: a historic reserve of some of the earliest meetings of Māori and Europeans, Cook among them. The track climbs to a saddle lookout over the outer and inner sound.

points.name: Endeavour Inlet
points.note: First night at the head of the inlet (15 km, 5 h): lodges and a campsite. Panels recall the 1880s antimony mines.

points.name: Camp Bay
points.note: Second night: DOC campsite and lodges at Punga Cove, after 11.5 km round Big Bay.

points.name: Kenepuru Saddle
points.note: Road access and the start of the ridge: from here views over both Queen Charlotte and Kenepuru sounds. Private land pass needed.

points.name: Torea Saddle
points.note: Third night after the longest day (24.5 km): Cowshed Bay campsite or lodges at Portage below the saddle.

points.name: Anakiwa
points.note: Over Te Mahia Saddle and old bridle paths past Davies Bay to the jetty by the Outward Bound school; bus or boat to Picton.
